items.title: David Weiss interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 3, 2022
items.q: I think Bob Belden did one or two and Bob Mintzer did a couple. And they threw me a couple. And that’s the first time I think I wrote for that size band and I liked it.

ctx.x: Wow. Well we’ve been at it for about an hour and it’s very fascinating. I wanted to get one question in. If you had a tune, let’s say you started it at the piano or something, and then you went for a walk and you start I don’t know if you do this or not but maybe you’re arranging it in your head thinking of the possibilities. What is the sweet spot for you as far as how many voices you have to work with?

Wow. Good question. I’m going to say five. That’s what I settled on. I mean I guess my patter about this has changed. There was a point where I could say look I never wrote a big band chart except for my final in college. You know? It never interested me in that way. I like small groups and I think the path I took and how — I settled on octet because, it was actually a Freddie Hubbard thing. Freddie was having his chop problems, he owed a record company a record. I was working with the producers and we were, you…
